claim: Requests non-SysEx Web MIDI access and lists connected inputs and outputs.
sandbox: Open /demo/connect with a standards-shaped MIDI device and observe the permission request and selected ports.

claim: Sends cue lights only after opt-in, as note-on and note-off messages on the selected channel.
sandbox: Open /demo/connect with a standards-shaped MIDI output, opt in, select channel 2, and inspect the sent messages.

claim: Keys 1–4 and Space can run response practice.
sandbox: Open /demo, start with Space, play the first four sample cues with keys 1–4, then stop with Space.

claim: Routine editing limits routines to 1–64 steps and tempos to 40–240 BPM.
sandbox: Open /demo/arrange, reach both step limits, reject 39 BPM, and save at 240 BPM.

claim: Exports versioned Pad Light JSON and validates imports under 100 KB.
sandbox: Open /demo/arrange, inspect an exported file, import a valid routine, and reject an oversized file.

claim: Routines save in browser storage and survive a reload.
sandbox: Open /demo/arrange, save a named routine, and reload the same demo workspace.

claim: Works offline after the first visit.
sandbox: Use a new browser context at /demo, wait for the service worker, go offline, reload, and play the first cue.

claim: The free sample flow needs no account and sends no product requests off this origin.
sandbox: Record all browser requests during a /demo practice and arrange flow, then verify one origin and no account fields.
